draft.title: Fossil fuels and biofuels
card: a fuel formed from the remains of ancient organisms over millions of years. Coal, natural gas and petrol are fossil fuels.
a fuel made from recently living material, such as plants, algae or animal waste. Biogas, bioethanol and biodiesel are biofuels.
Fossil fuels take millions of years to form, so they are non-renewable on any human timescale. Biofuels can be replaced quickly by natural processes, such as crops growing each season.
Both kinds store chemical energy and release it when they burn. What separates them is the source and how fast the source is replaced.
draft.remember: Fossil fuels come from ancient remains and take millions of years to replace. Biofuels come from recent living material and are replaced quickly.

a.q: Why is natural gas classed as a fossil fuel rather than a biofuel?
opts: It formed from ancient organisms over millions of years
It is made from crops that regrow each season
It is a gas, and biofuels are always liquids
It releases chemical energy when it burns
a.why: Natural gas formed from the remains of ancient organisms over millions of years, so it cannot be replaced quickly. Releasing energy on burning is true of both fossil fuels and biofuels, so it does not separate them.
a.clue: Think about the source and how long it took to form.

b.q: Kofi's farm in Mildura turns pig manure into methane-rich gas to run a generator. Which type of fuel is this gas?
opts: A biofuel, because the source is replaced quickly
A fossil fuel, because it is a gas like natural gas
A fossil fuel, because it contains methane
A biofuel, because it is made without any burning
b.why: The gas is biogas, made from animal waste, which is recent living material that is replaced quickly. Being a gas or containing methane does not make a fuel fossil, as the source is what counts.
b.clue: Look at where the gas came from, not what it is made of.

a.best: It formed from ancient organisms over millions of years

b.best: A biofuel, because the source is replaced quickly
